questions.question: Which ancient text, attributed to the sage Vyasa, is a central epic of ancient India and consists of 100,000 verses in 18 parvas (books)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mahabharata**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The Mahabharata was originally known as the Jaya Samhita. 
 
• It was a shorter epic version, consisting of only 8,800 verses. 
 
• It was written by the sage Vyasa and focused on the events leading up to and including the Kurukshetra War.
 
• The Jaya Samhita was later expanded by Vyasa's disciple Vaisampayana, who added 15,200 verses. 
 
• This expanded version of the epic was called the Bharata, and it was the first time that the story of the Mahabharata was told in its entirety.
 
• The Bharata was further expanded by other authors over the centuries, and it eventually grew to its current size of over 100,000 verses. 
 
• This final version of the epic is known as the Mahabharata.
 
• The name "Jaya Samhita" means "Collection of Victories". 
 
• It is thought that this name was chosen because the epic focuses on the victory of the Pandavas over the Kauravas in the Kurukshetra War.
 
• The Mahabharata is one of the longest epics in the world, and it is a major part of Hindu culture. 
 
• It is a complex and fascinating story that has been told and retold for centuries.

questions.question: Under the influence of the Greeks, which of the following art styles flourished in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gandhar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Gandhar art style is heavily influenced by Greek art, particularly after the conquests of Alexander the Great.
 
• This art form flourished primarily in the regions of present-day Afghanistan and Pakistan during the 1st to 5th centuries CE.
 
• Gandhar art is characterized by intricate carvings, realistic human figures, and the use of motifs such as Greek gods and mythological beings.
 
• The most significant contributions of Gandhar art are the numerous sculptures of the Buddha, which exhibit a blend of Indian and Greek artistic elements.
 
• The Gandhar style played a crucial role in the spread of Buddhism through its expressive and detailed representations of the Buddha and Buddhist narratives.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kushan Empire:** The Gandhar region was under the control of the Kushan Empire, which facilitated the synthesis of Greek and Indian art forms.
 
• **Iconography:** Gandhar art is noted for introducing the iconic representation of the Buddha in human form, prior to which he was represented by symbols.
 
• **Materials Used:** Artists in the Gandhar region commonly used materials like grey schist and stucco for their sculptures and architectural decorations.
 
• **Architectural Influence:** The architectural style of Gandhar includes elements like Corinthian columns and acanthus leaf decorations, reflecting Greek influence.
 
• **Spread of Gandhar Art:** Gandhar art significantly influenced the art and culture of Central Asia, China, and other parts of Asia through the Silk Road.

questions.question: Which of the following was the first language conferred with the status of Classical Language in India?

questions.question: In which of the following regions of India is the Mundari language spoken?

questions.question: Which is the second largest family in modern Indian languages?

• Dravidian languages are spoken in** southern and central India,** as well as parts of Sri Lanka, Pakistan, Nepal, and Bangladesh.
 
• The Dravidian language family includes languages** like Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, and Malayalam.**
 
• The largest family in modern Indian languages is Indo-European (Aryan), which includes languages like Hindi, Bengali, Punjabi, and Marathi.
 
• Sino-Tibetan (Kirata) and Austric (Nishada) are also language families in India, but they are smaller in size compared to Dravidian and Indo-European.
 
• Sino-Tibetan languages are spoken in the northeastern parts of India, while Austric languages are spoken in central and eastern India.

questions.question:
With reference of Ajivikas, consider the following statements.

a) Makkhali Gosala was the prominent teacher of this sect.

b) Ajivikas believed in fatalism.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both a and b**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Makkhali Gosala** was indeed the prominent teacher of the Ajivika sect, which is a fundamental point in understanding the history of this ascetic sect.
 
• The Ajivikas were known for their belief in **fatalism**, the idea that all events are predetermined and therefore inevitable.
 
• The sect was a contemporary of Buddhism and Jainism and had a significant influence during the time of the Mauryan Empire.
 
• Ajivikas followed a strict ascetic lifestyle and believed in the concept of niyati (destiny).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ajivikas:**

 
 
• The Ajivikas were an ascetic sect that emerged in ancient India around the same time as Buddhism and Jainism. They believed in the doctrine of predetermination, where every event is preordained and humans are powerless to change their destiny.
 
• **Makkhali Gosala:** He was one of the key figures in the Ajivika sect. His teachings emphasized the power of fate over individual effort.
 
• The teachings of the Ajivikas were based on the principle of niyati, which means destiny. This doctrine suggested that everything in the world was predetermined and fixed, and human efforts to change their fate were futile.
 
• The Ajivikas practiced extreme asceticism and renunciation, similar to other contemporary religious movements like Jainism.
 
 
 
• **Fatalism:**
 
 
• Fatalism is the philosophical doctrine suggesting that all events are predetermined and inevitable, a belief that is central to the Ajivika philosophy.
 
• It implies that human actions have no effect on the future, which is already decided by destiny or fate.
 
• This belief can lead to a deterministic outlook on life, where individuals accept whatever happens without trying to change their circumstances.
 
• In the context of Ajivikas, this meant that their ascetic practices were part of adhering to their predetermined path.

• Ashoka's reign (circa 268–232 BCE) is known for the construction of numerous stupas and pillars as part of his efforts to spread Buddhism across India.
 
• The Ashokan pillars were made of polished sandstone, not granite or marble.
 
• These pillars often featured inscriptions detailing Ashoka's edicts and policies, which were written in Prakrit and other languages.

• It starts on the fourth day, or chathurthi, of **Bhadrapada**, the **sixth month in the Hindu calendar**, which runs from **August to September.**
 
• Ganesha idols are set up on elevated platforms in houses or in ornately decorated outside tents before the beginning of the celebration.

• **Kartika,** the eighth month of the Hindu calendar, is also the seventh month in India's national civil calendar, spanning from October 23 to November 21 in the Gregorian calendar.
 
• **Ashadha,** the fourth month of the Hindu calendar, aligns with June or July in the Gregorian calendar, starting from June 22 to July 22.
 
• **Vaishakh, **the second month of the Indian national calendar, corresponds to April or May in the Gregorian calendar.

questions.question: What is the State religion of Maldives?
questions.solution:

__
 
• The state religion of the Maldives is Sunni Islam.
 
• The 2008 Constitution established Islam as the official religion of the country.
 
• T he constitution also states that citizenship is based on adherence to Islam, making the country's citizens 100% Muslim. 
 
• It is illegal to promote any religion other than Islam.
 
• Penalties for violating this regulation include house arrest, imprisonment, or deportation.

• **​**Christianity **constitutes a minority religion** within the Maldives.
 
• Scholar Felix Wilfred from Oxford University conducted research in **2013 estimating the Christian population** in the Maldives to be approximately 1,400 individuals, representing about 0.4% of the total population
 
 
 
• **Buddhism**
 
 
• **​**Buddhism was the** state religion of Maldives before 1153 CE**
 
• Buddhist relics and ruins of monasteries have been found in many islands.
 
• Additional **evidence of a Buddhistic past was found in late 12th** century copperplate grants, translated in the 1980s.
 
 
 
• **Hinduism**
 
 
• **​**Before **embracing Buddhism as their way of life,** Maldivians had practised an ancient form of Hinduism, ritualistic traditions known as Śrauta, in the form of venerating the Surya (the ancient ruling caste were of Aadheetta or Suryavanshi origins)
 
• Evidence **suggests that Hinduism **had a presence in pre-Islamic Maldives.
 
• Archaeological remains survive from the 8th or 9th century CE portraying Hindu deities such as Shiva, Lakshmi and the sage Agastya.
